headline: Approved architectural details for Orange Street & Pearl Street parking deck, 4 Bremer Street subdivision, and 30 Bryant Road subdivision extension.
summary: The meeting covered a 457-space parking deck and 125-unit apartment project at Orange Street & Pearl Street, which received approval of its architectural details. A waiver allowed a 15-foot sewer easement at 4 Bremer Street, and the subdivision there was approved. The conditional subdivision at 30 Bryant Road received a six-month extension, and eight new applications were found to have no regional impact.
decisions: Approved PDSP2024-002 compliance hearing for architectural details of the Orange Street & Pearl Street parking deck; motion carried with one recusal from Mr. Boyle.
Granted a waiver to allow a 15-foot sewer easement where 20 feet is required at 4 Bremer Street; motion carried.
Approved subdivision application S2026-016 at 4 Bremer Street with the Findings of Fact and staff recommendations, including 13 conditions; motion carried.
Approved a six-month extension for the 30 Bryant Road subdivision, with conditions to meet expiring March 6, 2027; motion carried.
Approved finding that eight new applications do not have regional impact and do not warrant review by the Manchester Conservation Commission; motion carried.
Approved minutes of August 20, 2026, as written, with one abstention; motion carried.

(Motion Carried with one recusal from Mr. Boyle)

 Findings of Fact: 109 
1. Section 6.7 of the Subdivision and Site Plan Review Regulations establishes a 110 
 minimum 20-foot easement width for sanitary sewer and stormwater pipes 111 
 located outside of streets. An existing private easement provides the abutting 112 
 property with rights of ingress and egress to lay, maintain, service, and repair 113 
 the existing sewer that crosses proposed Lot 13A. 114 
2. The existing private easement does not specify the width of the area that may be 115 
disturbed for maintenance or repair. The garage referenced in the easement is 116 
proposed to be removed as part of the development of proposed Lot 13A. 117 
3. The approximate location of the existing sewer is shown on the subdivision plan 118 
based on available sewer card information; however, the exact location and 119 
depth of the sewer have not been field verified. The proposed three-unit 120 
residential building shown on the ZBA exhibit plan is in close proximity to the 121 
approximate location of the existing sewer. 122 
4. Jacobs Engineering has advised that a 20-foot easement is appropriate as a 123 
general standard, but that a narrower area may be appropriate based on site-124 
specific information, including the location and depth of the pipe and soil 125 
conditions. The applicant has provided professional information indicating that 126 
the proposed building could be constructed within approximately five feet of the 127 
existing sewer without structural issue. 128 
5. During technical review, EPD and Jacobs Engineering found the proposed 15-129 
foot easement for the new sewer service from Bremer Street acceptable based on 130 
the proposed location of that service and its relationship to the existing house. 131 
The existing sewer serving the abutting property is different in that its exact 132 
location and depth have not been field verified and its existing easement does not 133 
specify a width of protection or disturbance. 134
